screening_decisions.reason: This is an RCT comparing pre-emptive antifungal therapy (based on beta-D-glucan biomarker) vs no treatment in elderly critically ill surgical patients. The intervention is untargeted (pre-emptive based on biomarker, not proven infection). Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.

This is an RCT comparing prophylactic antifungal agents (clotrimazole, ketoconazole, nystatin) vs no therapy in critically ill adult surgical and trauma patients. The intervention is untargeted prophylactic treatment. Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.

This is an RCT comparing single-dose fluconazole prophylaxis vs placebo in patients with intra-abdominal perforations (critically ill surgical patients). The intervention is untargeted prophylactic treatment given before proven infection. Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.

This is an RCT comparing enteral fluconazole prophylaxis vs placebo in critically ill surgical ICU patients. The intervention is untargeted prophylactic treatment. Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.

This is an RCT comparing antifungal therapy vs placebo in critically ill patients with suspected ventilator-associated pneumonia and Candida colonization. The intervention is empiric/untargeted treatment based on colonization rather than proven invasive infection. Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.

This is an RCT comparing SDD regimen (including amphotericin B as antifungal component) vs standard treatment in critically ill ICU patients. While primarily targeting bacterial decontamination, the regimen includes antifungal prophylaxis. Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.

This is an RCT comparing preemptive anti-Candida treatment based on corrected colonization index vs usual care in critically ill patients. The intervention is untargeted preemptive treatment based on colonization markers. Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.
This is a literature review/systematic review, not an RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion.
This is a retrospective matched case-control study, not an RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion.

This appears to be a Cochrane review article (not an individual RCT) focusing on very low birth weight infants/neonates. The population may also fall outside the target population of critically ill adults and older children.
This is a prospective cohort study, not an RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion.

This is an RCT comparing empirical antimycotic therapy vs preemptive therapy (based on galactomannan test) in critically ill patients. Both arms represent untargeted strategies (treating without proven infection). Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.
This is a prospective surveillance/observational study, not an RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion.

This is an RCT comparing BDG surveillance with preemptive anidulafungin vs empiric antifungal treatment in ICU patients. Both arms represent untargeted strategies. Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.
This is a prospective cohort study developing a scoring system, not an RCT. There is no antifungal intervention. Does not meet study design or intervention criteria.
This is a consensus statement from an expert panel, not an RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion.

While this is an RCT using ketoconazole, the intervention is testing ketoconazole as a thromboxane synthetase inhibitor for ARDS prophylaxis, not as an antifungal agent. The study objective does not relate to preventing fungal infections.
This is a surveillance program report, not an RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion.
This is a meta-analysis of RCTs, not an individual RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion for primary studies.
This is a retrospective study, not an RCT. Does not meet the study design criterion.
This is a clinical guideline document (ESCMID guideline), not a randomized controlled trial. Guidelines do not meet the RCT study design requirement.

RCT comparing caspofungin prophylaxis (untargeted antifungal) to placebo in high-risk critically ill ICU adults. Meets all criteria: RCT design, antifungal prophylaxis intervention, critically ill non-neutropenic population.

While this is an RCT, the intervention is selective decontamination of the digestive tract (SDD) which is primarily an antibiotic prophylaxis regimen (polymyxin, tobramycin, cefotaxime) with amphotericin B as a minor component. The study focuses on bacterial decontamination, not specifically antifungal prophylaxis.
This is a retrospective analysis/cost-of-illness study, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT study design requirement.
This is a retrospective study developing a clinical prediction rule, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT study design requirement.

RCT comparing fluconazole (untargeted antifungal) to placebo in critically ill adult ICU patients with septic shock. Meets all criteria: RCT design, antifungal prophylaxis intervention, critically ill non-neutropenic population.
This is a cost-of-illness analysis using secondary data sources, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT study design requirement.
This is a systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs, not a primary randomized controlled trial. Reviews do not meet the RCT study design requirement.

RCT comparing antifungal prophylaxis (garlicin or fluconazole) to control in patients with severe acute pancreatitis (critically ill, non-neutropenic). Meets all criteria: RCT design, antifungal prophylaxis intervention, critically ill population.
This is a matched case-control study, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT study design requirement.

RCT comparing fluconazole prophylaxis to placebo in high-risk surgical patients with recurrent GI perforations/anastomotic leakages (critically ill, non-neutropenic). Meets all criteria: RCT design, antifungal prophylaxis intervention, critically ill population.
This is a consensus conference document providing definitions and guidelines for sepsis, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT study design requirement.

RCT comparing oral amphotericin B prophylaxis to placebo in ICU patients with serious infection (critically ill, non-neutropenic). Meets all criteria: RCT design, antifungal prophylaxis intervention, critically ill population.
This is a prospective population-based surveillance study, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT study design requirement.

RCT comparing pre-emptive antimycotic therapy to treatment only with proven invasive candidiasis in general ICU patients (critically ill, non-neutropenic). Meets all criteria: RCT design, antifungal intervention, critically ill population.

While this is an RCT, the intervention is primarily antibiotic prophylaxis (norfloxacin, polymyxin E, cefotaxime) with amphotericin B as a minor component. The study focuses on preventing respiratory tract infections, not specifically fungal infections.

While this is an RCT with ketoconazole, the intervention is for anti-inflammatory treatment of ALI/ARDS, not for antifungal prophylaxis. The study objective is to test ketoconazole's anti-inflammatory effects, not antifungal effects.
This is a meta-analysis of RCTs, not a primary randomized controlled trial. Reviews do not meet the RCT study design requirement.
This appears to be a Cochrane review (based on abstract ending). Additionally, the population is very low birth weight infants, not critically ill adults/children as specified in the protocol.
This is a prospective observational study, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the RCT study design requirement.
This is a surveillance/observational study, not an RCT. It describes epidemiology of nosocomial BSIs but does not test antifungal interventions.
This is a systematic review of RCTs, not a primary RCT. Additionally, it focuses on children with prolonged fever and neutropenia, which excludes them from the non-neutropenic population.
This is a retrospective cohort study, not an RCT. It examines timing of treatment in patients with confirmed candidemia rather than testing untargeted prophylaxis.
This is a systematic review/meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. Cancer patients post-chemotherapy/HSCT are typically neutropenic, outside the target population.

This is a double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT comparing empirical fluconazole vs placebo in adult ICU patients at high risk for invasive candidiasis. Population is non-neutropenic critically ill adults.
This is a meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. While liver transplant patients may be critically ill, this is a secondary analysis.
This is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT specifically in nonneutropenic critically ill patients comparing fluconazole vs placebo for prevention of Candida infections.
This is about antibiotic prophylaxis, not antifungal prophylaxis. The intervention does not match the review question.
This is a retrospective cohort study, not an RCT. It examines timing of treatment in patients with confirmed candidemia rather than untargeted prophylaxis.
This is a meta-analysis, not a primary RCT. While it analyzes relevant RCTs, it is itself a secondary analysis.
This is a Cochrane systematic review focusing on cancer patients with neutropenia. The population (neutropenic cancer patients) is outside the scope.

This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT in NICU/PICU patients (pediatric critically ill) comparing fluconazole vs placebo. These are non-neutropenic critically ill children.
This is an economic/cost analysis study, not an RCT. It does not test antifungal interventions.
This is a pilot, open-label, prospective study comparing treated patients to historical matched controls, not a randomized controlled trial.
This is a point prevalence observational study, not an RCT. It describes epidemiology of infections in ICUs.
This is an observational autopsy study, not an RCT. It examines correlation between Candida isolation and pneumonia.
This is a clinical practice guideline document, not an RCT. It provides recommendations based on evidence review.
This is an observational study comparing diagnostic tests, not an RCT testing antifungal interventions.
This is a prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT in critically ill surgical patients comparing ketoconazole vs placebo for prevention of yeast colonization/invasion.
This is a retrospective cohort study, not an RCT. It examines outcomes in patients with confirmed Candida septic shock.

This is a diagnostic test review analyzing mannan antigen and anti-mannan antibody tests for diagnosing invasive candidiasis. It reviews 14 retrospective studies, not an RCT comparing antifungal treatments.

While this is a prospective randomized controlled trial comparing fluconazole prophylaxis vs no prophylaxis, the population consists of peritoneal dialysis patients with chronic kidney disease stage 5, not critically ill ICU patients as required by the protocol.
This is a multicenter observational cohort study collecting epidemiological data on intra-abdominal candidiasis. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing antifungal interventions.
This is a single-center observational report describing the emergence of echinocandin-resistant Candida isolates. It is not a randomized controlled trial comparing antifungal treatments.
This is a retrospective analysis of the EPIC II prevalence study examining Candida bloodstream infections in ICUs. It is an observational study, not a randomized controlled trial.
This is a prospective cohort study examining Candida colonization and subsequent infections in critically ill surgical patients. It is observational in design, not a randomized controlled trial.

This is a prospective randomized controlled trial comparing oral nystatin (nonabsorbable antifungal) prophylaxis vs no nystatin in mechanically ventilated critically ill ICU patients. The population matches (critically ill, non-neutropenic), and it compares untargeted antifungal treatment vs no antifungal.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing amphotericin B in lipid emulsion vs amphotericin B in dextrose solution. However, both groups receive antifungal treatment (different formulations of the same drug), not antifungal vs placebo/no antifungal/another antifungal as required by the protocol.

This is a randomized controlled trial comparing oral nystatin prophylaxis vs control in surgical/trauma ICU patients. The population matches (critically ill, non-neutropenic), and it compares untargeted antifungal treatment vs no antifungal.
This is a review article published in The New England Journal of Medicine summarizing trends and strategies in invasive candidiasis. It is not a randomized controlled trial.
